what: specs/aw_monthly.yaml (AdventureWorks monthly review, report month 2013-11) drafted by two in-region Bedrock models (ap-south-1), read sentence by sentence against the query rows. 'wrong_claims' are statements the number checker cannot catch: every number was real, but a ranking, a comparison or a meaning was wrong. One run per row; the spec changed between rows as noted.

failures: decisions and trend not drafted: JSON cut off at 700 tokens (a 13-month, two-series section cites 26 numbers)
runs.fix: draft token limit now scales with the numbers a section offers (draft.draft_max_tokens)

runs.spec_state: token fix; model asked to rank and compare
wrong_claims: decisions: 'sold $2.7 million below cost' ($2.7M was the sales; the margin was -2.7%)
trend: internet peak placed in 2013-06 (it was 2013-11)
trend: reseller called the steadier channel (it is the more volatile one)
territories: Northwest called the largest growth (Germany, 536.8%)
territories: Germany called the slowest growth (Southeast, 30.1%)
categories: Clothing called the lowest margin (Components, 6.4%)
runs.fix: rankings moved into the SQL as labels (note columns: 'fastest growth', 'lowest margin', 'highest internet month'); prompts say: use only the notes, do not rank

wrong_claims: decisions: 'sold $2.7 million below cost' (flagged by the meaning check at the gate)
territories: Canada named with Germany as fastest growth (only Germany is labelled)
trend: 'highest month this month' for reseller (the prompt told every section to say 'this month', wrong for a trend)
checker_caught: '$0.5 million' for $537,955.52: rounding loses more than 5%, published as [unverified]
runs.fix: trend prompt names months as the rows write them; money below $1 million in thousands

checker_limit: '$0.3 million' for Germany passed because it matches Central's sales ($298,183.67) in the same query: the checker proves a number exists, not which row it belongs to; the gate's meaning check is the second line

readability: territories: sales amounts left out, 'a change in percent of 443.3'

conclusion: The fix that mattered was moving every ranking and comparison into the SQL: after it, both models made no wrong claims on the final spec. DeepSeek V3.2 reads better (scaled money, complete sentences) at about $0.009 per report against Gemma's $0.002; for a report a manager reads, that is the chosen model for this spec. Small samples: one to two runs per model on the final spec.
